G8896.d: 1. to send before, send on  or forward , [8th/7th c.BC]: also, to send  something to  another, ἀγγελίας, φήμην [8th/7th c.BC]:—; [8th/7th c.BC] often with an infinitive added; αἰετὼ προέηκα πέτεσθαι, οὖρον προέηκεν ἀῆναι [8th/7th c.BC] 2. to send away, dismiss, let go , [8th/7th c.BC]; τήνδε θεῷ πρόες let  her go  to the god, i. e. in reverence to him, [8th/7th c.BC] 3. to let loose, let fall , especially thoughtlessly, ἔπος προέηκε let drop  a word, [8th/7th c.BC]; πηδάλιον ἐκ χειρῶν προέηκε he let  the helm slip  from his hands, [8th/7th c.BC]; δάκρυα προῆκεν [Refs 5th c.BC] 4. of missiles, to send forth, shoot  or dart forth , [8th/7th c.BC] 5. of a river, ὕδωρ προί̈ει ἐς Πηνειόν it pours  its water into the Peneius, [8th/7th c.BC] 6. πρ. τινί ποιεῖν τι to allow  one to do, [Refs 5th c.BC] 7. to give up, deliver over, betray  one to his enemy, [Refs 5th c.BC, Refs 5th c.BC]: —;Pass. to be given  or thrown away , εἰ προεῖτο ταῦτα [Refs 4th c.BC] 8. ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτίκα ἡδὺ πρ. αὑτόν to give up  or devote  oneself to present delights, [5th/4th c.BC] 9. Mid. to send forward from oneself, drive forward , [5th/4th c.BC]:—;of sounds, to utter , [Refs 4th c.BC], etc. 10. to give up, let go: to give up  to the enemy, [Refs 5th c.BC], etc.; πρ. σφᾶς αὑτούς gave  themselves up as lost , [Refs 5th c.BC] 11. to desert, abandon , [Refs 5th c.BC]; οὐδαμῆ προί̈εντο ἑαυτούς did  not lose  themselves (i. e. take bribes), [Refs 4th c.BC] 12. to give away, give freely , [Refs 5th c.BC], etc.; προέσθαι ἀπὸ τῶν ἰδίων [Refs 4th c.BC] 13. to throw off  one's clothes, [Refs 4th c.BC]: and, in bad sense, to throw away , τὸν καιρόν [Refs 4th c.BC]; τὰ πατρῷα [Refs 4th c.BC]: absolute to be lavish , [Refs 4th c.BC] 14. a second predicate is sometimes added, ἡμᾶς προέσθαι ἀδικουμένους to suffer  us to be wronged, [Refs 5th c.BC]; προέμενοι αὐτοὺς ἀπολέσθαι [5th/4th c.BC]; πρ. τινὶ ὑμᾶς ἐξαπατῆσαι [Refs 4th c.BC] 15. to suffer to escape , [Refs 2nd c.BC] 16. rarely in good sense, to give over  to one, confide to one's care , [5th/4th c.BC] 17. to neglect, disregard , [Refs 4th c.BC]:—; absolute to neglect all advice, to be reckless , [Refs 4th c.BC] (ML)

G8897.d: 1. to set before;  so in Mid., [5th/4th c.BC] 2. Pass., with aorist2  and perfect active, φυλακῆς μὴ προκαθεστηκυίας no guard having been set beforehand , [Refs 5th c.BC] (ML)

G8898.d: 1. to seize beforehand, preoccupy , [Refs 5th c.BC], etc.:—;Pass. to be preoccupied , [Refs 5th c.BC] 2. metaphorically to anticipate, frustrate , [Refs 5th c.BC, Refs 4th c.BC]:—;of persons, to anticipate  or surprise  them, [Refs 5th c.BC] 3. to overpower before , [Refs 5th c.BC] (ML)
